items.text: Qatari mediators are seeking US and Iranian backing for a draft that sets out a three-day sequence of confidence-building steps and could restart direct talks within days. Iran called Washington's reply to its Hormuz conditions "not convincing" and wants the blockade lifted and sanctions eased first. Vice President [[p:JD Vance]] has reportedly reached out to [[p:Mohsen Rezaei]]. Brent fell to about $93.6 on 5 Nov, then rebounded to about $98 on 6 Nov.

US forces carried out what officials called "limited, defensive" strikes on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on 2 Nov, after the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] fired on a US aircraft. Tehran said it keeps the right to self-defence. An Indian-flagged cargo ship was struck off Oman on 3 Nov, killing one crew member. (Missed in the 5 Nov log.)
items.notes: US account of the trigger is attributed to US officials.

items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on 5 Nov: two hit naval mines and a third caught fire. No independent confirmation yet.

[[p:Donald Trump]] met Russian envoy [[p:Kirill Dmitriev]] in Washington on 5 Nov, ahead of the 10–11 Nov Abu Dhabi talks, and predicted a "big" agreement that would go beyond Ukraine and "might involve all of Europe". He gave no details. [[p:Volodymyr Zelensky|Zelensky]] says the midterm result improves the odds of new US aid.

The death toll from Russia's 2 Nov strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia oblast, rose to 43, with 33 still missing. Bombs, including a FAB-3000, hit a school where residents were collecting aid, then a shelter and arriving rescuers.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Toll per Zelensky and national police; not yet final.

items.text: The [[p:United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara|UN mission in Western Sahara (MINURSO)]] {{note: Set up by the Security Council in 1991 to monitor the Morocco–Polisario ceasefire and organise a referendum that never took place.}} ended after 35 years. On 30 Oct Russia vetoed a US draft that backed Morocco's autonomy plan (11–1–3), and a Russian one-year rollover got only 3 votes. The mandate lapsed on 31 Oct and the UN began liquidating the mission on 1 Nov.

The [[p:Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic|SADR]]'s foreign minister, Mohamed Yeslem Beissat, said Russia's veto "saved" self-determination, called Morocco's autonomy plan dead for now and warned that "the alternative to diplomacy is war". Rabat says the ceasefire still holds without the mission: Foreign Minister [[p:Nasser Bourita]] calls it a political and legal commitment.
items.outlet: Middle East Eye; Morocco World News

items.text: The third Russia–Africa summit in Moscow (28–29 Oct) adopted a joint action plan for 2027–29 covering trade, health and humanitarian aid. Moscow extended its infectious-disease programme for Africa to 2029 and promised more grain and student places. [[p:Vladimir Putin]] backed a permanent African seat on the UN Security Council.

The Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic has now killed more than 5,300 people since May. The [[p:Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention|Africa CDC]] counts 10,444 confirmed cases in DRC and calls it the fastest-growing outbreak in the country's history. [[p:World Health Organization|WHO]] experts approved trials of two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines, including one from Oxford, the Serum Institute and Moderna; results are expected in early 2027. A British health worker who was infected is being evacuated.

UN humanitarian coordinator Denise Brown says recent drone strikes appear to be systematically destroying power stations, fuel depots, markets and displacement sites. A strike near Khartoum halted dialysis for 25 patients. Hundreds of aid trucks are stranded by fuel shortages, and [[p:World Food Programme|WFP]] is cutting rations and caseloads.

Heavy fighting west and southwest of El Obeid ([[e:Siege of El Obeid]]): the army-allied Joint Force says it took Umm Samima, Kazgil, Al-Hamadi and Abu Qud, destroying 40 [[p:Rapid Support Forces|RSF]] vehicles and capturing 43. The RSF released videos claiming it still holds all four. Neither side's claim is confirmed.
items.notes: Darfur24 publishes in Arabic and English; the English edition was used.

items.text: Sudan hit back for the Asosa expulsions by closing Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref and expelling its diplomats. The row is over Khartoum's charge that Ethiopia lets the RSF launch drones from its territory; Addis Ababa denies it and accuses Sudan of backing the [[p:Tigray People's Liberation Front|TPLF]].

A Sudanese government report says 70 drone attacks using 187 one-way drones were launched from Ethiopian territory between February and October, 28 of them in October, from sites including Asosa airport and the Bahir Dar airbase. Sudan's Sovereignty Council says drones killed 176 soldiers and 484 civilians from 15 Feb to 27 Oct. None of this has been independently verified.

The [[p:Ethiopian National Defense Force|federal army]] imposed a night curfew on vehicles in Mekelle (8pm–6am) from 7 Nov. It ordered unlicensed guns handed in within three days and announced house-to-house searches, blaming prisoners it says the TPLF freed and criminal gangs.

The US Embassy says fighting continues in Tigray's Central Zone and in remote areas near the Eritrean border. Flights to Axum and Shire remain suspended, and US citizens are told to leave Tigray, Amhara and Afar. An Ethiopian state minister again alleged Eritrean incursions, which are unverified.
items.outlet: US Embassy Addis Ababa; Wazema Radio

items.text: The Ethiopian Orthodox Church reports fresh killings in Robe district (Arsi), after an attack last month that reportedly killed about 60. The state rights commission separately reported 48 deaths in Shirka district last month, which it blamed on the [[p:Oromo Liberation Army]] and informal armed men.
The Ethiopian Media Authority suspended the weekly The Reporter, and the [[p:Committee to Protect Journalists]] condemned the move.
Ethiopia asked a visiting EU Political and Security Committee delegation to ease deforestation (EUDR) and carbon-border (CBAM) rules that hit coffee and cocoa exporters.

South Kivu civil society groups say fighting broke out this week in the hills around Uvira, then eased, as the Kabila-led FRN rebellion pushes on the city on the Burundi border. On 27 Oct the FRN claimed villages within 7 km; the army and the governor denied any advance. About 12,000 households have reportedly fled Kaziba.

Counting is under way after the 4 Nov local elections (29.2 million registered), seen as a test of the [[p:African National Congress|ANC]], which polls put below 40%. Partial counts show the [[p:Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|DA]] on about 40% in Johannesburg and [[p:Jacob Zuma]]'s [[p:uMkhonto weSizwe Party|MK]] leading in KwaZulu-Natal. Official results are due on 8 Nov.

MK organiser Lastborn Shazi was shot dead at home in KwaZulu-Natal on the eve of the vote. Police count 20 political killings during the campaign, and Ramaphosa deployed more than 500 soldiers to the province.
Gunmen ambushed a police convoy near Gidan-Giye in Zamfara's Tsafe area, killing at least eight police and vigilantes and abducting others, local officials say.
